analysis.title: Few charts
key_insights: Clients aggressively sold protection on Wednesday as markets rallied, then scrambled to buy it back the next day.
The Vol Panic index surged to 9.57 out of 10 on Thursday. The 5% increase was the 3rd largest daily jump ever.
The GS AI basket (GSTMTAIP) had its worst day since Covid on Thursday. The desk calls the move macro driven, citing exploding ETF volumes.
Prime data shows global equities de-grossing for a 4th straight session (8 of the last 9), though Thursday's pace of risk unwinds was relatively modest.
Global equities saw the largest net selling in two weeks (-1.6 SDs 1-year), driven by long-and-short sales (2.2 to 1).

Global AI stocks were net sold for a 6th consecutive session (-2.6 SDs 1-year). Hedge fund selling of global AI stocks over the trailing 20 days is the largest in more than five years (-3.0 SDs 5-year).
AI-related volatility has taken over from energy prices as the primary driver of directional yield moves.
Growth and momentum factors sold off while Value outperformed. The Risk Appetite Indicator is at -0.7 (momentum at -1.2).
GS Global Investment Research argues for strong visibility on US data center construction growth through 2028, backed by 28GW under construction and a $900bn high-confidence pipeline.
GIR raised its 2026/27 data center spend forecast to $80bn/$100bn and introduced $125bn for 2028.
US data center capacity under construction should rise from 65GW-gross in 2026 to 143GW-gross by 2030. Texas is 20% of 2027E net additions and 27% of 2028E.
Consensus expects European EPS growth of 23% y/y in 3Q26, with most sectors seeing positive earnings revisions since the start of October.
The GS strategy team raised its STOXX 600 EPS growth forecasts to 18% for 2026 and 7% for 2027, and introduced 5% for 2028.
US-listed ETFs had their third largest notional volume day in the dataset at $580 billion, 33% of the tape versus a 28% average. Friday volumes ran at 36% of the tape and +65% vs the 20-day average.
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Thursday in prime books, the largest 1-day increase since March, led by Large Cap Equity ETFs.
Technology is 43% of US earnings but 7% in Europe. The ten largest US companies account for 40% of index earnings.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds net sold global AI stocks for six straight sessions and the GS AI basket had its worst day since Covid. This is flow commentary, not a formal rating.
Value outperformed while growth and momentum sold off. This is a factor performance observation, not a formal rating.

Most European sectors have seen positive 2026 EPS revisions since 30 September 2026.

risk_factors: AI-related volatility is now driving directional yield moves, replacing energy prices.
Continued AI stock selling by hedge funds, at the fastest 20-day pace in more than five years.
Risk appetite has fallen significantly over the last month, with momentum weaker still.
Elevated ETF short interest and record ETF volumes point to macro-driven positioning stress.
